chunks: So he turned away from them and said: "O my people, I have conveyed to you the messages of my Lord, and gave you good counsel; so how can I grieve for a people who do not believe?"
ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Shu'aib say to his people before turning away from them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the transition of Prophet Shu'aib from active preaching to patient waiting (tawqif), emphasizing that his duty was merely conveyance (tabligh) and sincere advice (nasihah). The rhetorical question 'How can I grieve for a disbelieving people?' underscores the spiritual detachment required when the audience remains obstinate, a principle often applied to the Ahl al-Bayt's relationship with the Ummah. This moment marks a critical shift where the prophet's personal emotional investment yields to divine decree, reinforcing the concept of 'balagh' as the completion of the message regardless of reception.
